topic: Software Catalog adds an incorrect www. prefix to GitHub repository URLs translated from a Backstage annotation
product_area: Software Catalog (Backstage catalog-info.yaml ingestion via the GitHub integration)
environment: Backstage catalog-info.yaml files ingested into Software Catalog
symptom_pattern: A Backstage catalog-info.yaml with a github.com/project-slug annotation is ingested by the GitHub integration and translated into Software Catalog format. The resulting repository location has a www. hostname, but repository entities in Software Catalog have no www. As a result the service is not linked to its repository entity. This shows up as broken Source Code linking, DORA metrics unable to infer the repository, and a false report that the GitHub integration is not set up.
root_cause: The translation of the Backstage github.com/project-slug annotation into a Software Catalog repository location added a www. prefix to the GitHub hostname. Engineering confirmed this and merged a change to remove the www. prefix. The rollout reached the customer's environment later because of slow deployments during an internal incident.
resolution_path: Support confirmed the behavior was incorrect and escalated it to engineering.
Engineering merged a change that removes the www. prefix from GitHub repository URLs.
The customer edited a catalog-info file after the merge and the code location still had www., because the change had not yet been deployed to their environment.
Support confirmed the change was later deployed in the customer's environment, and the customer verified that a re-ingested catalog-info file now produced the correct URL.
Existing catalog-info files were only re-ingested when modified, so support triggered a re-sync of the whole software catalog on the customer's behalf.
The customer confirmed everything was refreshed and working.

qa_pairs.tse_question: Would you like us to trigger the ingestion process for your entire software catalog for your org?
qa_pairs.customer_answer: Yes, the customer asked for a full re-ingestion of their whole software catalog.

qa_pairs.tse_question: Engineering says a re-sync is possible in the UI. Can you use it?
qa_pairs.customer_answer: The customer did not have the Re-Sync button in their account, so they asked support to start the re-sync for them.

customer_style.tone: polite, collaborative, and persistent about the business impact on DORA metrics adoption

tse_approach.summary: The support engineer reproduced the behavior, agreed with the customer that it was a bug, and escalated it to engineering. They kept the customer informed through a slow rollout, then arranged a catalog-wide re-sync for the customer.
steps: Tested the reported behavior and confirmed it was incorrect.
Asked the code-security team in Slack and escalated to engineering through a Jira card.
Updated the customer when the fix was merged.
Investigated why the customer's test edit still showed www. and found the deployment was delayed by an internal incident.
Confirmed when the change was deployed to the customer's environment.
Checked with engineering about re-ingesting the whole catalog and triggered the sync on the customer's behalf.
Told the customer when the Re-Sync UI button was expected to be available for their region.
key_questions: Would the customer like support to trigger the ingestion process for the entire software catalog?
communication: Gave regular status updates through the escalation and explained that the delayed rollout was caused by an internal incident. Offered the full re-sync proactively and told the customer when to retest. Gave the Closed-after-5-business-days policy and a way to reopen.
